source.title: K-Bench: A Benchmark for LLM Unlearning in Agentic Deployments
source.authors: Guangsheng Yu; Yanna Jiang; Qin Wang; Baihe Ma; Xu Wang

page_placements.theme: Agents, context memory and tools resupply or retain forgotten information

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether unlearning results hold under an agentic, multi-channel observer and argues that low leakage can reflect channel migration, refusal, or agent collapse rather than removal. It also tests a held-out paraphrase condition, but not most recovery attacks in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many outcomes, but results about unrelated research, layer-selection diagnostics, and methods' composite leaderboard scores were not entered unless they directly measured leakage or the rephrasing condition. The activation-editing experiments attempt suppression; they do not ablate a direction after unlearning to test recovery. The paper tests paraphrasing only as a query-form change, not jailbreaks or other languages.
record.test_reason: The study applies a WMDP-style forced-choice MCQ and other direct-elicitation probes to weight-unlearned models, alongside a multi-channel agent observer. Functional recipes keep the secret recognisable (MCQ 0.86–1.00), and low leakage elsewhere comes with agent or model collapse. This is a result that version A is wrong or partial. It also tests one held-out paraphrase as a prompt-only recovery attack (E) and reports FLAT's resistance to it (F).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that single-channel, parametric evaluation overstates unlearning for agents. Weight-based recipes either leave the secret directly elicitable (MCQ 0.95–0.98) or suppress it only by collapsing the agent. Only oracle-gated input corruption (ECO) reaches selective forgetting, and the secret stays in the weights. FLAT blocks extraction on Llama without verified removal. No evaluated method demonstrably removes the secret, and the top method changes across bases. Correction: ECO's Llama terminal-collapse label reflects that base's 50.5% baseline degeneration, not collapse caused by ECO.
record.recipe_differences: K-Bench is an agentic multi-channel evaluation benchmark, not a reproduction of the cited original methods. It ports and evaluates multiple published methods, with disclosed adaptations, on synthetic PII and real-format LUME records.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by base model, substrate, observer channel budget, method, injection strength, and query phrasing. The paper reports that FLAT resistance differs by base, that the leading method changes across bases, and that attacker verdicts can change when additional channels are observed.

fits_no_version.finding: On structured retrieval, StaR cuts answer-channel leakage from 0.832 to 0.463 while tool-observation leakage stays at 0.857. Aggregate leakage is unchanged.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Output-filter unlearning in agents migrates leakage to unmonitored channels rather than removing it.

fits_no_version.finding: Weight probes (TOFU, MUSE, MCQ, MIA) read chance on context and retrieval substrates while the agent leaks on 22–86% of queries.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model-level unlearning certificates miss non-parametric leakage in deployed agents.

fits_no_version.finding: Under ECO on retrieval, most forget answers disclose another individual's true record. Counting forget-set third parties roughly doubles leakage, to 0.11–0.16.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input-corruption unlearning can substitute disclosure of other entities for the target.

record.code_released: saberyu.pro/kbench; GitHub reference in text: OniReimu/kbench
record.problems: The paraphrase ladder uses n=200 per cell and reports no uncertainty for its paired differences; on some bases, degeneration changes substantially between phrasings. The study does not test most recovery attacks in the claim. Synthetic PII is the main test corpus; real-format validation covers only date of birth. The paper notes that its substrate-P injection uses LoRA and does not test pretraining memorization. Some low leakage results coincide with agent collapse, and ECO's query gate uses ground-truth forget membership in the reported reference setup.
record.rows_left_out: Did not enter the full activation-editing grid in Table 9 because it evaluates interventions intended to suppress leakage, not post-unlearning activation ablation as a recovery attack. Did not enter the twenty-method K-Score roster in Table 11 as individual rows because those composite scores do not separately report the specific recovery behaviors in the claim; the paper's FLAT paraphrase outcomes are represented from Table 18. Other channel budgets, API-served models, and retrieval-substrate results were omitted because they do not test fine-tuning, quantization, or the specified prompt-only recovery attacks.

untested.parts: Resistance of any method to fine-tuning, quantization, jailbreak or other-language attacks. Only one held-out paraphrase was tested, and not for ECO.
Not tested: no relearning or fine-tuning attack after unlearning.
Not tested: no post-unlearning direction ablation and no internal analysis distinguishing blocking from deletion. ECO's weights are untouched by construction, which is not a finding.
Jailbreaks, other languages and in-context information. Only one held-out paraphrase, at n=200 and seed 0, on substrate P.
FLAT's resistance to fine-tuning, quantization, activation ablation, jailbreaks and languages. FLAT was tested only against the paraphrase and the completion probe.

missing.what: TOFU model-utility (MU) values per recipe and the retrain-only Gold reference (MCQ 0.11–0.14). These are needed to judge A's 'keeps general ability' part.
Llama P rows for StaR (OR 0.312, K-REF 2×), Cha (OR 0.175, retain 0.737 to 0.183) and O3 (OR 0.000 under a perfect oracle, 0.348 at oracle accuracy 0.50).
FLAT declarative-completion probe on Llama: no-intervention base leaks 70%, FLAT holds 0% verbatim. Text only.
Summary-channel probe for NPO+KL/NPO: graded severity 0.545/0.293, full extraction on 40%/17% of forget queries.

record.verdict_notes: Many E rows were mislabelled 'reversed' for negligible decreases. The study's run-to-run spread is 0.04, so these are absent. Collapsed cells (100% degeneration) are unreadable. ECO rows were wrongly linked to C, since keeping the weights untouched is ECO's design, not a finding. StaR on R-struct concerns retrieved data, not model knowledge. Whether FLAT counts as a 'robust counter-method' under F is debatable: the paper frames it as refusal-tuning, not a robustness claim.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures target leakage, retain behavior, and agent stability for evaluated methods, and compares several direct-elicitation probes. It does not test all attacks named in the claim, nor establish that knowledge is removed from weights.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack using unrelated, loosely related, or subset examples.

The paper explains that ECO corrupts inputs while leaving weights untouched and says FLAT's resistance does not verify removal. It does not test post-unlearning activation-direction ablation as a recovery attack or directly measure recovered internal knowledge.
Tests a held-out paraphrase of the canonical query on substrate P. Does not test jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information as recovery attacks.

Tests FLAT under the held-out paraphrase/query-form condition and reports extraction resistance for Llama-3.1-8B. It does not test resistance to the fine-tuning, activation-ablation, or quantization attacks, or to jailbreaks and other languages.
